title: SDK examples kits and snippets roadmap (sketch)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working sketch for a compact, opinionated set of SDK examples, tiny sample apps, and language-specific quickstarts that we can ship with the SDK packages and reference in the Console quickstart. Goal is to lower time-to-first-success for engineers evaluating Redwood: 2-minute install, 5-minute sample, 10-minute end-to-end flow with telemetry and error handling baked in.

Audience:
- Product engineers trying Redwood for the first time
- Developer advocates creating sample apps and tutorials
- Internal SDK maintainers who need canonical snippets for docs and tests

Scope (what we will include in v1 kit):
- Minimal quickstart examples in Python, Node (TS), Go and Rust (one-liners + small app)
- A tiny CLI example that uses hosted API key + environment variable config
- One interactive chat example and one embeddings + vector search example per language
- Minimal telemetry hooks (request id, latency, token cost) and sample logs
- A tests folder with 3 smoke tests (generation, streaming, embeddings) that can run on CI with a dev key
- README template for each language that shows config, sample output, and FAQ/troubleshooting

Constraints / non-goals:
- We will not ship full-blown sample apps (no full stack boilerplate) in v1. Keep examples single-file where possible.
- We will not include enterprise-only features (Dedicated routing configs, VPC instructions) in the public quickstart.

Deliverables & layout (proposed):
- /examples/python/quickstart.py  # one-file generation example
- /examples/python/chat_bot/  # 3 files: client.py, run.sh, README.md
- /examples/node/quickstart.ts
- /examples/go/quickstart.go
- /examples/rust/quickstart.rs (small binary using reqwest)
- /examples/cli/  # tiny CLI referencing SDKs and showing env var config
- /examples/shared/README-TEMPLATES.md
- /tests/smoke/  # small scripts that call examples with test key

Sketch: quickstart behaviors (Python example)
- Install: pip install redwood-sdk (or from local wheel)
- Environment: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
- quickstart.py:
  from redwood import Client
  client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  resp = client.generate(model='open-mosaic-1', prompt='Write a 2-sentence summary of Redwood')
  print(resp.text)

- Include note: if streaming is supported, show two modes: immediate and streaming. Example will default to non-streaming to keep simple.

Node/TS sketch (quick):
- npm i @redwood/inference
- quickstart.ts shows fetch-like API and an example with function calling placeholder

Go sketch (notes to self):
- Use native http client with minimal wrapper; show example where token counting is approximated using response.
- Provide simple config file snippet: ~/.redwood/config.yaml for defaults (region, model, api_key)

Rust sketch (notes):
- Keep crate dependency list tiny (reqwest, serde_json). Provide sample for toggling sync/async.

CLI example (single-file in /examples/cli):
- Usage: redwoodctl generate --model open-mosaic-1 --prompt "Summarize my README"
- Config precedence: CLI flags > env vars > ~/.redwood/config.yaml
- Telemetry: print request-id on each run and exit code semantics (0 success, 2 API error, 3 network)

Telemetry & Observability (very small):
- Examples must emit minimal structured logs: timestamp, request_id, model, prompt_len, latency_ms, tokens_consumed (if returned), status_code
- Provide a short code snippet showing how to attach a callback/hook to record per-request metrics to an in-process histogram (prom-client for Node, prometheus_client for Python)
- Include guidance in README for enabling verbose logging: REDWOOD_LOG=debug

Error handling guidance (in samples):
- Basic retry policy for 5xx with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
- Token-limit errors: show graceful fallback to a shorter prompt and helpful user message
- Quota errors: show sample instructions to check Console > Billing > Usage

Testing & CI guidance:
- Small test harness that uses a short-lived dev key (circles back to DX-1345 for automated test keys)
- Tests should assert successful HTTP 200 and non-empty text or embeddings vector length > 0
- Add a note: avoid flakiness by mocking network in most tests; keep smoke tests opt-in using env var RUN_SMOKE=true

Docs & README template (for each language):
- Quick start section (install, set key, run sample)
- What you just saw: explanation of fields in response, tokens, streaming vs non-streaming
- Troubleshooting checklist (network, auth, region mismatch, rate limit)
- Contributing: how to add an example, coding style, test expectations

Rollout plan + timeline (rough):
- Week 1: implement Python and Node single-file quickstarts + README templates (owner: Marcelo)
- Week 2: add CLI and Go example (owner: Aisha)
- Week 3: Rust example + integrate smoke tests into examples repo (owner: Jordan)
- Week 4: docs review, copyedit, add Confluence page + link to Console quickstart (owner: Evelyn)
- Post-launch: gather telemetry from Console quickstart flows and iterate on examples that show common errors

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which default model to recommend in public examples? (open-mosaic-1 vs smaller optimized model) -- CC: research/Applied ML on model cost/latency tradeoffs
- Should we include conversation state helpers in SDK examples or leave as separate utility package?
- Decide whether to include an example that demonstrates deduped streaming + prefix caching (probably too advanced for v1)
- DX-1345: short-lived test keys for CI — follow up with security for acceptable limits

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep code formatting minimal; avoid heavy idiomatic patterns that complicate copy/paste for beginners
- Make one canonical Python snippet that we can copy to Console quickstart - single file, < 25 lines
- Add small screenshot/ASCII output examples to README for clarity

References / links: see linked_artifacts above. Also keep an eye on GH PR 472 for API surface changes that might require snippet updates.

Quick todo (immediate):
- [ ] Draft python quickstart.py and validate locally with dev key
- [ ] Create README-TEMPLATES.md with placeholders for common sections
- [ ] Create CI smoke job that is gated by RUN_SMOKE=true and documents steps to request a dev key
- [ ] Sync with research on recommended public model and update examples accordingly

End of sketch. This is intentionally terse and pragmatic — goal is to produce small, copy-pasteable examples that reduce friction for new users.
